title: Usage pacing and chargeback smoothing: PRD for billable burst reconciliation and entitlements bridging
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers report unpredictability when burst usage spikes near the end of billing cycles. Current model bills overage immediately which causes billing surprises and accounting churn. This PRD defines a usage-pacing and chargeback smoothing feature: allow customers to opt into a 'pacing window' that smooths per-cycle overage charges, provides a true-up flow, and enables entitlement bridging across plan transitions (upgrade/downgrade) without immediate invoice spikes. Scope includes API semantics, console UX, metering windows, accounting rules for true-ups, and acceptance criteria for billing accuracy. Out of scope: wholesale changes to existing metering primitives, partner marketplace billing (handled separately).
requirements: Add a customer opt-in flag 'billing.pacing_window' (30/7/1 day options) that defers overage charges into a smoothing bucket within the invoice period
Implement entitlement bridging: when customers upgrade mid-cycle, map consumed units to previous plan rates and calculate incremental charge or credit in a true-up line item
Support scheduled true-up invoice generation at period boundaries (configurable: at cycle end or next invoice date)
Provide console UI to visualize pacing bucket, projected overage, and estimated true-up before invoice finalization
Expose API endpoints for retrieving pacing status, projected charges, and to opt-in/out programmatically
Ensure metering telemetry and ledger entries provide immutable audit trail for reconciliations and support export to accounting systems (CSV/GL mapping)
Define fallback billing behavior if pacing is disabled mid-cycle: immediate invoice + retrospective credit reconciliation
Integrate with rate-limit enforcement: pacing should not relax hard concurrency limits, only billing timing changes
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer with an active pacing window, overage usage during the window is recorded to a smoothing bucket and not billed on immediate invoice runs
At cycle boundary, system generates a single true-up line item that calculates net owed amount (or credit) using per-model rates, proration, and any applied discounts
When a customer upgrades mid-cycle, consumed tokens map to original plan for historical usage and policy generates correct incremental charge for remainder of cycle
Console shows projected true-up within +/- 2% of the generated invoice for a sample of test accounts (10 accounts with mixed burst patterns)
API endpoints return pacing status and projected charges with latency under 200ms for 95th percentile queries
Ledger exports contain stable identifiers linking meter events -> smoothing bucket -> invoice line item for full reconciliation
Billing shard and accounting team have testable CSV export that matches invoice totals for test cases including discounts, coupons, and prorations
Security review completed and no sensitive tokens are leaked via pacing endpoints or console logs
tradeoffs_and_notes: Tradeoff: Deferring charges increases complexity in collections and may require cashflow adjustments for finance; mitigated by opt-in model and configurable windows
Tradeoff: Smoothing may make short-term revenue recognition more complex; work with accounting to define recognition rules for true-ups
Note: This PRD avoids touching marketplace billing. Marketplace partners will be considered in a follow-up epic
Note: We will reuse existing metering primitives; metering events are immutable and assigned attributes to mark 'smoothing.bucket' for visibility
Decision: Hard rate-limits remain enforced in real-time; pacing affects invoicing only, not throttling behaviors
Open question: whether to allow per-route vs account-level pacing windows. Default to account-level to reduce complexity; evaluate per-route in a later cycle
test_plan: Unit tests for pacing flag behavior and ledger assignment
Integration test: simulate end-of-cycle true-up for 50 synthetic accounts with varied burst patterns and validate invoice totals
E2E test with console: enable pacing, run synthetic usage, verify projected true-up and final invoice matches expectations
Load test: 10k pacing status API calls per minute; verify 95th percentile latency <200ms
Accounting reconciliation test: CSV export matches GL entries for test cohort
implementation_milestones: M1: Schema/enumeration for pacing windows and ledger attribute additions (ENG sprint 1)
M2: API endpoints + backend routing for smoothing bucket assignment (ENG sprint 2)
M3: Console views and projected true-up calculation UI (DES + ENG sprint 3)
M4: Billing engine true-up generation and CSV/GL export (ENG + Finance sprint 4)
M5: Security review, compliance sign-off, and pilot with 3 customers (Pilot week)
M6: Launch and post-launch rollback/playbook documentation (Ops)
